title: Christie Brinkley shares how she keeps her three adult children coming home
text:

Christie Brinkley, star of ‘American Summer,’ explains why losing both parents made family time more precious and shares how she keeps her children close.

Christie Brinkley never really had to face an empty nest.

The actress and supermodel stars opposite Steve Guttenberg in "American Summer," a feel-good tribute to simpler times and family connections.

The 72-year-old told Fox News Digital those themes aren't just on-screen. They're values she's embraced in her own life, creating a home her three adult children can still return to.

The movie, which hit theaters Sept. 4, follows Guttenberg's character as he looks back on a formative childhood summer filled with baseball, first love and the disappearance of his U.S. Army father overseas.

CHRISTIE BRINKLEY HAS FANS MISTAKING SUPERMODEL FOR DAUGHTER IN NEW PHOTOS

Christie Brinkley's new movie, "American Summer, hit theaters Sept. 4. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"I have always been all about family, so I have built my life in a way that my kids. ... I want them independent," Brinkley said. "I want them out there living, doing whatever, but they always tend to come home on weekends, holidays. We all really are big on being together, and I love that.

Christie Brinkley and daughters Sailor Lee Brinkley-Cook and Alexa Ray Joel arrive at the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit 2017 launch event at Center415 Event Space in New York City Feb. 16, 2017. (GC Images)

"It's funny because a lot of moms on Instagram will ask me, 'How do you get your kids to come home so often? Mine are off and about,'" the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover girl shared.

"And I think it's just to always let them know they're always welcome back. They can bring their friends, that kind of thing."

Christie Brinkley's children — Alexa Ray Joel, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook and Sailor Brinkley-Cook — remain a central part of her life. (Getty Images)

The supermodel is often photographed alongside her three grown children — Alexa Ray Joel, 40, Jack Paris Brinkley-Cook, 31, and Sailor Brinkley-Cook, 28 — whether they're walking red carpets or stepping out in coordinated looks. Brinkley said their close bond didn't happen by accident but was rooted in the example set by her own parents.

WATCH: CHRISTIE BRINKLEY SHARES SECRET TO KEEPING HER FAMILY CLOSE

After losing both of her parents less than two months apart in 2012, Brinkley said she no longer takes family time for granted. Her father, Don Brinkley, died July 14, followed by her mother, Marge Brinkley, on Sept. 9.

"I have always cherished my family time," Brinkley said. "And I think once you lose both of your parents, it becomes more precious because you know that there is a finite time to it. And right now, our family's smaller because I don't have my mom and dad."

Alexa Ray Joel and Christie Brinkley appear onstage at the Big Apple Circus in New York City Feb. 1, 2020. (Getty Images for Big Apple Circus)

Brinkley became visibly emotional before saying, "I always get choked up whenever I talk about them."

Christie Brinkley's parents attend a pageant in Hawaii, date unknown. (Corbis via Getty Images)

Guttenberg is no stranger to Brinkley's heartbreak. He became a caregiver for his father, Stanley Guttenberg, after he developed kidney failure, eventually training to help administer dialysis at home.

"I remember you telling me about your mom and dad, Christie, that you had a little house on your property, and they lived near you, right?" Guttenberg said. "Isn't that wonderful? How lucky you were and are to have them right there. It's priceless, right? ... The greatest thing in the world."

Family came first for Steve Guttenberg, who paused his acting career to help care for his father, Stanley Guttenberg. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"The best," Brinkley replied. "My parents were always, always so ready to be there for me. Good times, bad times, they were always there, and they always made an effort to be a family. And I think it's so important, and it has given me my happiest moments."

"American Summer" is described as a homage to families in small-town America. (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

Family continues to be an essential part of Brinkley's life. She shared that Alexa Ray was preparing for a concert that night, while Jack planned to attend the premiere of "American Summer" alongside her.

For Brinkley, the movie's message extends beyond the screen. She believes audiences are craving stories that celebrate family.

Christie Brinkley and Sailor Brinkley Cook attend the Solving Kids Cancer Annual Hamptons Luncheon at Tutto II Giorno in Southampton, N.Y., on Aug. 4, 2025. (Sonia Moskowitz/Getty Images)

"People want to put down their phone and speak to another human face to face," she said. "This [story] takes us back before there were cellphones. And I think that we're going to find people now putting down their cellphones more often and just connecting with loved ones.

"And that human connection, nothing can replace it. I find that whenever I light a little bonfire in the backyard or at the beach. I always say, 'This is it. This is free. This is simple. And you know what? This is as good as it gets.'

Steve Guttenberg and Christie Brinkley in a scene from "American Summer." (Blue Harbor Entertainment)

"Just to be able to sit there by the crackling of the fire, the moon coming up, the stars sparkling, the birds chirping, the crickets coming on, the fireflies lighting — that's it," she continued. "That's the best. Slowing down the speed of life, human connections. ... I think those are things that we all want to feel again and again."

"It's better than any Ferrari," Guttenberg said.

Christie Brinkley poses with son Jack at the opening night arrivals for Michael Moore's "The Terms of My Surrender" on Broadway at the Belasco Theatre in New York City Aug. 10, 2017. (Bruce Glikas/FilmMagic)

Brinkley's love of simple pleasures doesn't stop with family gatherings. She's also an avid birdwatcher, a hobby she believes is making a comeback as more people look to unplug.

Christie Brinkley attends Best Friends Animal Society's The Spirit of the Sanctuary"benefit Aug. 24, 2026, at Jill Rappaport's Last Buck Ranch in Water Mill, N.Y. (Getty Images)

"I've always been a birdwatcher," she said. "On my Instagram, I have a bird feeder, and if you go back, you'll see lots and lots of pictures of the birds at my bird feeder. And I was just reading that birdwatching is back in full force for young people, too. People want to connect with nature. They want to get in nature, and it's all part of just that slowing down."
